exercise.name: Smith Incline Close Grip Bench Press
aliases: Smith machine incline close-grip bench press

reference.title: Smith Incline Close Grip Bench Press
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace as you lower the bar, hold it through the touch, breathe out as you press.
breathing.cadence: About 2.0 s down, 0.3 s touch, 1.2 s up

prescription.tempo: 2-0-1-0 (2 s down, no pause, 1 s up)
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9). Expect a little less than your regular bench press: the narrow grip gave the lowest loads in Saeterbakken 2021.
prescription.progression: Add reps up to the top of the range, then add 1.25-2.5 kg.

cues.text: Set the back pad to about 30 degrees and place the bench under the Smith bar so it lines up with the upper chest; glutes in the crease, feet planted. Grip overhand about shoulder width, turn the bar off the pegs and hold it up with straight arms.
Breathe in and lower the bar to the upper chest, elbows tucked close to your sides (about 20-30 degrees from the body).
Touch the chest lightly, no bounce; elbows stay tucked, wrists straight over the forearms.
Breathe out and press straight back up the rails, driving the elbows straight.
Arms straight, re-brace and go again; after the last rep turn the bar back onto the pegs.

mistakes.mistake: Hands too close together (thumbs almost touching)
mistakes.fix: Grip about shoulder width; a very narrow grip strains the wrists and does not add triceps work.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flaring out to the sides
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows tucked close to the ribs so the triceps do the pressing.

mistakes.mistake: Wrists bent back under the bar
mistakes.fix: Stack the bar over the heel of the palm, wrist and forearm.

mistakes.mistake: Bouncing the bar off the chest
mistakes.fix: Lower under control and touch lightly before pressing.
Keep the glutes on the bench and the feet planted.

kinematics.peak: Buttocks in the crease, upper back and head on the pad (rig shapes); trunk 67° from vertical
kinematics.norm: Back pad at about 30 degrees; 30 degrees gave the highest upper-pectoralis activity, above it the anterior deltoid took over (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020); Lauver 2016 recommends 30 degrees

kinematics.setup: 36 cm between the bar grips (shoulder joints 39.9 cm apart)
kinematics.norm: About shoulder width or a little inside it; narrow grips raised triceps activity and lowered the load lifted (Saeterbakken 2021)

kinematics.setup: ≈9° at the top (arms straight, not locked)
kinematics.norm: Arms straight but not locked at the top; elbows deeply bent with the bar on the chest (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Arms reaching up to the bar
kinematics.peak: ≈22° from the trunk at the bottom; upper arms ≈38° below the back plane
kinematics.norm: Upper arms about 20-30 degrees from the trunk at the bottom, close to the ribs (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Vertical Smith rails 18 cm toward the feet from the shoulder joints; top 80.5 cm above the bench
kinematics.peak: Bottom on the upper chest (bar resting on the rig chest shapes), 44.3 cm of travel straight down the rails
kinematics.norm: Fixed by the vertical rails: straight down to the upper chest and straight back up (common coaching)
Feet flat on the floor with the knees bent about 90 degrees, like the bench set-up in Solstad 2020

kinematics.peak: 2 s down, 0.3 s at the bottom, 1.2 s up, 0.7 s at the top
kinematics.norm: Controlled: about 2 s down and 1-2 s up (clinical opinion; Rodríguez-Ridao 2020 used 2 s down and 2 s up)

cautions: Set the safety stops just under the lowest bar position before the first rep; the bar cannot go lower than them.
Practise turning the bar on and off the pegs (a small turn of the wrists) with an empty bar first.
The rails fix the bar path: place yourself so the movement feels natural for the joints, and do not force range.
Line the bench up so the bar meets the upper chest before you load it.
Wrist pain: widen the grip slightly so the forearms are closer to vertical (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Wrist or elbow discomfort: a slightly wider grip, or an EZ bar.
Shoulder discomfort: shorten the range at the bottom (board or floor press).
regressions: Floor press with a close grip.
progressions: Steeper incline (45 degrees) for more shoulder work.

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Main elbow extensor: triceps activity was higher with a narrow barbell grip than a wide one (Saeterbakken 2021; Muyor 2023: about 16% vs 12% of MVIC at 50% vs 150% of shoulder width); triceps activity did not change with bench angle (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Main elbow extensor: triceps activity was higher with a narrow barbell grip than a wide one (Saeterbakken 2021; Muyor 2023: about 16% vs 12% of MVIC at 50% vs 150% of shoulder width); triceps activity did not change with bench angle (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.pec_r: Presses the arms up; the 30-degree incline shifts the work toward the upper (clavicular) fibres (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020). Grip width did not change overall pectoralis activity in the flat bench press (Saeterbakken 2021).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Presses the arms up; the 30-degree incline shifts the work toward the upper (clavicular) fibres (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020). Grip width did not change overall pectoralis activity in the flat bench press (Saeterbakken 2021).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder; it works harder as the bench rises and was about as active as the upper chest at 30 degrees (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Flexes the shoulder; it works harder as the bench rises and was about as active as the upper chest at 30 degrees (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the shoulder blades against the rib cage as the bar is pressed.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Holds the shoulder blades against the rib cage as the bar is pressed.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: A minor stabiliser; less active with a narrow grip than a wide one (Saeterbakken 2021).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: A minor stabiliser; less active with a narrow grip than a wide one (Saeterbakken 2021).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blades drawn back and down on the bench.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Keep the shoulder blades drawn back and down on the bench.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the ribs down and the pelvis on the bench.

phases.label: Arms straight, bar over the shoulders

guides.label: Press back up over the shoulders
Elbows tucked and deeply bent at the bottom
